attrs.evidence: NOT PROVED, and R3.1 asserted it. It is plausible — probably true — and the only argument offered for it was invalid: FED-WITNESS-BOUND bounds the canonical construction from above and says nothing about how small a refutation can be, which FED-MIN-GROWS makes concrete. Establishing it needs a LOWER-bound family: languages whose MINIMUM refutation size diverges. Note the shape of what is required — not a language with a large canonical query, which is easy, but one where no small refutation exists at all, which is the hard direction and the reason this is a research question rather than a measurement.

attrs.review_focus: This is the load-bearing proposition behind "a bounded search can never decide the property", and nothing here establishes it. Any future claim that a bounded search is inconclusive IN GENERAL must cite this record, and this record is open.
attrs.statement: For every fixed search bound B there is a finite Γ that fails the gluing property but whose every refutation exceeds B.
